newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold bourse to start futures in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold bourse to start futures in 1997.

text.p: Istanbul Gold Exchange targets to begin futures and options trading at the start of 1997 to increase market turnover, its secretary general Kaan Aytogu said.

"After the publication of the regulations of the Istanbul Gold Exchange futures and options market on October 18, we speeded up our preparations. Our aim is to open this market at the beginning of 1997," Aytogu told Reuters.

"After the launch of the Exchange (in July 1995), a futures market will pave the way for the use of gold as an investment tool and increase depth in the domestic gold market. It will also offer hedging opportunities for the jewellery sector," he said.

He said the exchange would hold an extensive training programme for the bourse members between November 11-13 to inform them about the new market's infrastructure, technical details as well as trading rules.
The Exchange is working jointly with the Treasury and the Capital Markets Board (SPK) and in contact with international gold bourses in preparation for the futures and options.
"The bourse members will be trained and can start to trade in futures and options after they receive approval from the SPK and the Exchange," Aytogu said.
Currently, gold traded in dollar and lira terms in the morning session are settled and delivered the same day while afternoon deals are settled the following day.
Member banks are the main gold importers which sell it on the bourse or on the free market.
Turkey's gold demand was 25.1 tonnes in the first quarter of 1996, down from 31.7 tonnes in the last quarter of 1995 and compared with 11 tonnes in first quarter 1995.
Total 1995 demand was 112.5 tonnes after 38 tonnes in 1994.
